[Shot 1] From 00:00 to 00:09. The camera is on the gravel path level with her eyes, two long strides from her, a 50mm lens. The fanlight comes from BEHIND at the LEFT. At the first frame the Wife's head and shoulders fill the CENTRE of the frame from her chestnut hair at the TOP third to the paisley shawl at the BOTTOM edge, her head a third of the frame's height. The glowing fanlight sits at the LEFT third and the laurels are black at the RIGHT edge. The shot is inside this place: The front of the narrator's red-brick villa at Maybury on a warm starlit night in 1894: a black four-panel door with a brass knocker under a small tiled porch on two turned posts, a fanlight glowing, a lit bay window at the left, clipped laurels, a gravel path. The camera pans left across the whole shot, travelling a finger's breadth as the glowing fanlight keeps the left third, from 00:00 to 00:06. <Subject 1> (S1), on screen, oval face, with a clipped English voice at an even pace, says: <d>[English] Look, dear, the signal lights. Red and green and yellow. So bright.</d> Her mouth shapes every syllable as the line is heard and closes on the last word. At 00:06, as the line ends, her raised hand points toward the railway. At 00:08 her face turns to him with a smile, and the turn continues to the last frame of the shot. By 00:09 the camera is panning left through the last frame, and the action continues with it.
